title: Youth Apprenticeships, Daycare, Gang Prevention
summary:
*   **New Apprenticeship Programs:** Launched a multi-year Electric Department apprenticeship for disadvantaged youth (ages 18-23), offering training and a path to full-time city employment as Journeyman Electricians. An EMS apprenticeship was also discussed, alongside over 1,600 summer youth jobs.
*   **City Employee Daycare Initiative:** Explored establishing a year-round daycare program for city employees, specifically aimed at supporting limited-income families earning between $13,000-$19,000 annually.
*   **Youth Gang Prevention:** Discussed creating neighborhood-led programs to prevent gang involvement among 10-14 year olds, emphasizing community organization and early intervention.

Councilmember Garcia called to order the Special Called Meeting of the City Council
Opportunities for Youth Subcommittee, at 2:20 P.M.,noting the presence of Councilmember
Reynolds and Councilmember Larson. Mayor Todd arrived at 2:55 P.M., thus making it a
quorum of the Council. Councilmember Garcia announced the purpose of the meeting was as
follows: 1. Discussion of Opportunities for Youth Issue Paper recommendations
(two (2) hour session)
Alicia Perez, Assistant City Manager, introduced the discussion.
Before Mayor Todd arrived Ms. Perez outlined the Apprenticeship Program to be initiated by
the Electric Department. She told Council 10-12 youth, 18-23 years of age, will be in the
program for 4-5 years. After they have finished their training and sucessfully passed the
testing, they will become Journeyman, Electric and be employed by the City of Austin. This
program is designed to target disadvantaged youth with a certain amount of skills in the
field.
Subcommittee members directed that this item be put on the August 18, 1992 agenda of the
joint meeting with AISD Board.
Ms. Perez discussed the child abuse programs now in effect and said the topic will also be
dealt with in the next Legislative year.
Also discussed were the 1,644 youth who are in the employ of the City of Austin this
summer, as well as the EMS nine veek apprenticeship program.
When Mayor Todd arrived at 2:55 P.M., there was a quorum of the Council. At this point
Council discussed day care for City of Austin employees. They said a dollar amount must be
set year around, per family, for full time and part time care. The day care program will
be geared to limited income employees in the $13-19,000 bracket. Councilmember Reynolds
commented that the dollars spent on children need to be focused at an early age.
Councilmember Garcia said they need to look into neighborhood organizations getting
together and organizing programs for gangs in the 10-14 year old range.
The Council lost its quorum at 3:40 P.M., but discussion continued concerning the training
